approach: Split the journey into three phases of constant acceleration, powered rise, coasting rise, and free fall, and find the velocity and displacement at the end of each.

steps.text: Phase 1, powered flight for 5 s with acceleration 4 m/s² from rest: find the velocity and height reached.
Phase 2, after the fuel ends the rocket decelerates under gravity alone until its velocity reaches zero; find the time taken and the extra height gained.
steps.equation: Δt = 20/10 = 2 s (total t = 7 s), Δs = 20²/(2×10) = 20 m (total s = 70 m)

steps.text: Phase 3, the rocket falls freely from rest at 70 m under gravity; find the time to reach the ground.

The v-t graph rises from 0 to 20 m/s over 0–5 s, then falls to about −37.4 m/s by t ≈ 10.74 s, crossing zero at t = 7 s. The s-t graph rises from 0 to 50 m over 0–5 s, peaks at 70 m at t = 7 s, then falls to 0 at t ≈ 10.74 s.

final_answer.value: Rises to v = 20 m/s and s = 50 m at t = 5 s; coasts to the highest point s = 70 m at t = 7 s; falls back to the ground at t ≈ 10.74 s, landing at about 37.4 m/s

common_mistakes.text: Using the powered-phase acceleration of 4 m/s² instead of g = 10 m/s² for the coasting and falling phases, which changes the peak height and total time.
Forgetting to add the fall time to the 7 s already elapsed, reporting the total flight time as √14 ≈ 3.74 s instead of about 10.74 s.
